mission.title: Let's explore and define AI-assisted research together, as a community.
mission.intro: Brain Researcher (BR) is a collaborative research system for turning open scientific questions into shared, reviewable investigations. Researchers bring the starting point; BR helps refine the question, choose a first exploration, and bring evidence back for review.
mission.participation: Selected participants join the BR Autoresearch Consortium as active collaborators and co-authors on the consortium paper. Authorship reflects substantive contributions to the resulting work.

public_record.copy: Explore the public campaign and its research episode archive on GitHub.

future_direction.title: From exploration to experiment.
body: The longer-term goal is to carry a promising lead from the research landscape into a prospective real-world experiment: decide what should be tested, record the prediction before the result is known, and learn from what happens.

That experiment might be a behavioral task or game, a BCI session, an imaging study, an animal study, or wet-lab work. It would be designed and run by collaborating researchers and laboratories, with the result returning to inform the next question.

neuroimaging.title: Neuroimaging and brain measurement
neuroimaging.copy: The 111-topic source landscape remains searchable. A second layer groups the field into larger agenda directions shaped by the last decade of work on standards, reliability, scale, transport, naturalistic paradigms and causal measurement.
big_questions: What can be measured reliably across people, sessions and sites?
Which analysis choices change the scientific conclusion, and why?
How can measurement and experiment design improve before more data are collected?

agenda_directions.title: Open data, standards and reusable pipelines
agenda_directions.changed: BIDS and robust preprocessing pipelines made it possible to move datasets and analyses across laboratories without rebuilding every workflow from scratch.
agenda_directions.open: Standards still capture only part of the scientific intent, and reusable pipelines do not by themselves make analyses comparable.

anchors.title: The brain imaging data structure, a format for organizing and describing outputs of neuroimaging experiments
fMRIPrep: a robust preprocessing pipeline for functional MRI

questions.title: What scientific information must travel with a dataset for a new analysis to remain valid?
Which parts of a pipeline can be standardized without erasing legitimate methodological choices?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Audit public datasets and workflows, recover missing design information, and test whether supposedly equivalent pipelines produce equivalent scientific objects.

agenda_directions.title: Analytical variability and multiverse
agenda_directions.changed: Many-team studies and large-scale validation work made analysis choices observable rather than invisible.
agenda_directions.open: We still lack good ways to tell which choices change a conclusion, why they do so, and which differences are scientifically defensible.

anchors.title: Variability in the analysis of a single neuroimaging dataset by many teams
Cluster failure: Why fMRI inferences for spatial extent have inflated false-positive rates

questions.title: Which analysis choices carry the conclusion, and through what mechanism?
Can a smaller set of diagnostic analyses explain the larger multiverse?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Run bounded multiverses, decompose disagreement, and turn unexpected sensitivity into the next scientific question.

agenda_directions.title: Population-scale brain associations
agenda_directions.changed: ABCD, UK Biobank and other population cohorts made brain-behavior analysis possible at a scale that exposes small effects and heterogeneity.
agenda_directions.open: Large samples do not automatically solve leakage, site structure, confounding, weak effect sizes, or poor transport to new populations.

anchors.title: Reproducible brain-wide association studies require thousands of individuals
The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study: imaging acquisition across 21 sites

questions.title: Which associations stabilize with scale, and which disappear after better controls?
What sampling and measurement structure is needed before an association can guide a new study?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Reproduce effect-size curves, test held-out populations, and identify the smallest design that can separate signal from selection noise.

agenda_directions.title: Precision and individualized measurement
agenda_directions.changed: Dense within-person sampling showed that individual network organization can be measured rather than treated as residual variation.
agenda_directions.open: The field still needs to separate stable individual structure from state, motion, alignment error and measurement noise.

anchors.title: Precision functional mapping of individual human brains
Functional brain networks are dominated by stable group and individual factors, not cognitive or daily variation

questions.title: What can be measured reliably within a person that is lost in group averages?
How much repeated data is needed before an individual effect is worth interpreting?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Compare group, subject-specific and state-conditioned models under explicit repeatability and transport tests.

agenda_directions.title: Reliability across session and time
agenda_directions.changed: Large reliability studies made it clear that many familiar task and connectivity measures are less stable than assumed.
agenda_directions.open: Reliability is often treated as a property of a score, even though it depends on design, contrast, preprocessing, state and population.

anchors.title: What is the test-retest reliability of common task-fMRI measures?
A decade of test-retest reliability of functional connectivity: a systematic review and meta-analysis

questions.title: Which redesigns improve reliability without weakening construct validity?
When is an unstable measure still useful for prediction or intervention?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Search design and analysis variants against repeated measurements, with validity and nuisance controls kept in the objective.

agenda_directions.title: Cross-site, scanner and cohort transport
agenda_directions.changed: Harmonization methods and multi-site cohorts made transport a testable problem rather than a post-hoc nuisance correction.
agenda_directions.open: Removing site signal can also remove biology, and a method that works within known sites may fail on a new scanner or population.

anchors.title: Harmonization of resting-state functional MRI data across multiple imaging sites
Harmonization of cortical thickness measurements across scanners and sites

questions.title: What should be invariant across sites, and what should be allowed to change?
Can harmonization preserve a biological association in a site or vendor never seen during training?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Build leave-site and leave-vendor tests, compare adjustment targets, and identify where recalibration is unavoidable.

agenda_directions.title: Naturalistic and continuous paradigms
agenda_directions.changed: Shared naturalistic datasets made it possible to study language, memory and social cognition over minutes rather than isolated trials.
agenda_directions.open: Continuous stimuli create ambiguity about event boundaries, shared context, individual interpretation and the correct prediction target.

anchors.title: The Narratives fMRI dataset for evaluating models of naturalistic language comprehension
Single-trial neural dynamics are dominated by richly varied movements

questions.title: Which features of a continuous experience produce shared versus idiosyncratic neural effects?
How should events be segmented when the brain and stimulus do not share obvious trial boundaries?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Compare alternative event representations, align continuous behavior with brain data, and test predictions on held-out stories or viewers.

agenda_directions.title: Encoding, decoding and reconstruction
agenda_directions.changed: Modern language and vision models made rich stimulus reconstruction and prediction possible from non-invasive recordings.
agenda_directions.open: Strong reconstructions may rely on priors, subject-specific calibration or leakage rather than uniquely identified neural information.

anchors.title: Semantic reconstruction of continuous language from non-invasive brain recordings
Generic decoding of seen and imagined objects using hierarchical visual features

questions.title: What information is actually identified by the neural data rather than supplied by the generative model?
Which representations generalize across people, tasks and stimulus families?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Use matched-prior controls, cross-subject tests, and counterfactual stimuli to find where a decoder is reading the brain versus its own model.

agenda_directions.title: Multimodal and quantitative measurement
agenda_directions.changed: Large multimodal cohorts and cortical atlases made it possible to compare structure, function and physiology in a shared coordinate system.
agenda_directions.open: Modalities have different noise, scale and biological meaning; concatenating them does not guarantee a coherent measurement.

anchors.title: A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex
Multimodal population brain imaging in the UK Biobank prospective epidemiological study

questions.title: Which cross-modal relationships are stable enough to constrain a shared model?
When does adding a modality improve identification rather than add another confound?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Test modality ablations, measurement models and transport across acquisition environments.

agenda_directions.title: Clinical prediction and biomarkers
agenda_directions.changed: Large cohorts and predictive modeling made individual-level clinical claims more common.
agenda_directions.open: Many models still fail to improve decisions, generalize across sites, or distinguish prognosis from treatment selection.

anchors.title: A neuromarker for sustained attention from whole-brain functional connectivity
Reproducible brain-wide association studies require thousands of individuals

questions.title: What must a neural marker predict before it changes a clinical or experimental decision?
Which apparent subtypes survive external cohorts and alternative measurement pipelines?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Re-evaluate biomarkers on decision-relevant endpoints, external cohorts and explicit cheap baselines.

agenda_directions.title: Causal linkage to stimulation and perturbation
agenda_directions.changed: Lesion and stimulation network mapping created a bridge from correlational imaging maps to causal intervention sites.
agenda_directions.open: Convergence across modalities is incomplete, and network localization does not yet specify mechanism, timing or patient selection.

anchors.title: Brain stimulation and brain lesions converge on common causal circuits in neuropsychiatric disease
Closed-loop neuromodulation in an individual with treatment-resistant depression

questions.title: Which imaging effects make distinct causal predictions for stimulation or perturbation?
When do lesion, stimulation and observational maps point to the same circuit?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Translate imaging results into competing intervention predictions and rank the most discriminating validation experiment.

agenda_directions.title: Experiment and measurement optimization
agenda_directions.changed: Adaptive experiment design showed that data collection can be guided by a model rather than fixed entirely in advance.
agenda_directions.open: Optimization can chase a noisy objective, exploit a measurement artifact, or produce a design that is efficient but hard to interpret.

anchors.title: Neuroadaptive Bayesian optimization and hypothesis testing
What is the test-retest reliability of common task-fMRI measures?

questions.title: Which next stimulus, contrast or subject would reduce the scientific uncertainty most?
How should information gain be balanced against reliability, burden and interpretability?

agenda_directions.br_entry: Simulate candidate designs, predict disagreement between hypotheses, and freeze the most informative prospective test.

bci.title: BCI and neural interfaces
bci.copy: Over the last decade, BCIs moved from cursor-control demonstrations toward rapid communication, artificial sensation and brain-spine repair. The central challenge is now to keep the whole system useful as tissue, signals, hardware and users change.
big_questions: What becomes the bottleneck after a laboratory demonstration works?
Which neural variables remain usable as the brain, body, device and user all change?
How should recording, decoding, feedback and stimulation be optimized as one system?

directions.title: Biointegration and chronic materials
directions.changed: Ultraflexible probes showed that small, compliant devices can record for months while reducing the chronic tissue response.
directions.open: Delivery, packaging, connector failure, channel survival and the weak link between accelerated bench tests and long-term in-vivo performance remain major limits.

anchors.title: Ultraflexible nanoelectronic probes form reliable, glial scar-free neural integration
Neuropixels 2.0: a miniaturized high-density probe for stable, long-term brain recordings

questions.title: Which material and mechanical properties actually predict chronic channel survival?
Can an implant be stiff enough to place and tissue-like after deployment?
Which accelerated bench tests reproduce the in-vivo failure modes that matter?

directions.br_entry: Compare materials and device literatures, model coupled mechanical and electrical failure, and rank the experiments worth fabricating.

directions.title: Minimally invasive delivery and form factor
directions.changed: Endovascular and other lower-burden approaches widened the design space beyond penetrating arrays and scalp systems.
directions.open: Less invasive access often trades away spatial specificity, bandwidth or stimulation control, and the best route depends strongly on anatomy and function.

anchors.title: Minimally invasive endovascular stent-electrode array for high-fidelity, chronic recordings of cortical neural activity
Fully implanted brain-computer interface in a locked-in patient with ALS

questions.title: How much signal specificity can be retained as implantation becomes less invasive?
Which anatomy and task make an endovascular, surface, penetrating or peripheral interface the right choice?
Can delivery constraints be included before electrode geometry is chosen?

directions.br_entry: Map clinical use cases to access routes, compare signal and risk budgets, and simulate candidate form factors before device development.

directions.title: High-density sensing at useful scale
directions.changed: Neuropixels and integrated probes made simultaneous recordings from large populations and multiple structures routine in animal research.
directions.open: More sites can add redundant data, motion sensitivity, heat, bandwidth and analysis burden without increasing usable control information.

anchors.title: Fully integrated silicon probes for high-density recording of neural activity
Neuropixels 2.0: a miniaturized high-density probe for stable, long-term brain recordings

questions.title: When do additional channels add independent information rather than redundancy and instability?
How should site selection, on-device compression, power and thermal limits be co-designed?
What is the smallest recording scale that preserves the intended function?

directions.br_entry: Measure information gain per channel, compare site-selection policies, and connect hardware constraints to downstream decoding.

directions.title: Stable neural representations
directions.changed: Latent-space alignment showed that useful population structure can remain stable even when recorded units and waveforms change.
directions.open: It is often unclear whether drift comes from neurons, recording geometry, behavior, task strategy or the latent code itself.

anchors.title: Stabilization of a brain-computer interface via the alignment of low-dimensional spaces of neural activity
Neuropixels 2.0: a miniaturized high-density probe for stable, long-term brain recordings

questions.title: What is actually drifting: neurons, recording geometry, behavior or the latent representation?
Which latent variables remain identifiable across days and device changes?
When should a system align old and new spaces rather than relearn the task?

directions.br_entry: Decompose drift across repeated sessions, test invariant representations, and build falsifiable alignment controls.

directions.title: High-bandwidth intent decoding
directions.changed: Handwriting and speech neuroprostheses demonstrated communication rates and vocabularies that were not plausible a decade ago.
directions.open: Performance still depends on small participant numbers, calibration, task structure and powerful language priors, making the neural contribution hard to isolate.

anchors.title: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting
A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis
Neuroprosthesis for decoding speech in a paralyzed person with anarthria
A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control

questions.title: What limits communication rate after decoder accuracy becomes high?
Which neural representations support natural language, handwriting and continuous movement across contexts?
How much improvement comes from neural data versus language-model priors and interface design?

directions.br_entry: Run matched-prior ablations, compare representations and errors across tasks, and identify where another recording or model change would matter.

directions.title: Calibration, transfer and rapid adaptation
directions.changed: Cross-day alignment and shared population structure made reduced-calibration systems a realistic target.
directions.open: Transfer can silently import the wrong task, anatomy or user assumptions, and a few good calibration trials may hide later failures.

anchors.title: Stabilization of a brain-computer interface via the alignment of low-dimensional spaces of neural activity
Learning by neural reassociation
High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface

questions.title: What information transfers across sessions, tasks, participants or implants?
How little calibration is enough to know whether a model is safe to use?
Can adaptation distinguish neural change from device change?

directions.br_entry: Benchmark transfer at multiple shift levels, estimate calibration value, and define when the system should abstain or reset.

directions.title: Sensory encoding and bidirectional feedback
directions.changed: Intracortical stimulation produced localized touch and proprioceptive percepts, and artificial touch improved robotic-arm control.
directions.open: The field still lacks stable sensory codes that remain natural, informative and safe across electrodes, sessions and users.

anchors.title: Proprioceptive and cutaneous sensations in humans elicited by intracortical microstimulation
A brain-computer interface that evokes tactile sensations improves robotic arm control

questions.title: Which stimulation codes create stable, discriminable and useful percepts?
Does artificial feedback help because it conveys information, changes strategy or builds embodiment?
How should sensory and motor models co-adapt?

directions.br_entry: Model psychophysics and control together, compare coding schemes, and select stimulation tests that separate information from embodiment.

directions.title: User-system co-adaptation
directions.changed: BCI learning studies showed that users can reorganize neural activity to meet a decoder, rather than simply reveal a fixed intention signal.
directions.open: Algorithm updates can help the decoder while disrupting a mapping the user has already learned; user and machine learning are rarely measured together.

anchors.title: Learning by neural reassociation
Stabilization of a brain-computer interface via the alignment of low-dimensional spaces of neural activity

questions.title: Which changes should be assigned to user learning and which to algorithm adaptation?
When does decoder adaptation erase a mapping the user has learned?
Can training tasks shape a more stable neural control space?

directions.br_entry: Fit joint user-system learning models and compare adaptation schedules under matched task demands.

directions.title: Shared and supervisory control
directions.changed: Brain-controlled stimulation and bidirectional prostheses showed that autonomy can be distributed across user intent, device control and environmental sensing.
directions.open: Offline accuracy does not tell us when the machine should assist, yield, recover from error or preserve a users sense of agency.

anchors.title: Restoration of reaching and grasping movements through brain-controlled muscle stimulation in a person with tetraplegia
A brain-computer interface that evokes tactile sensations improves robotic arm control
Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface

questions.title: Which parts of an action should be controlled directly, predicted or automated?
How should autonomy yield when user intent and machine confidence disagree?
What evaluation captures agency and recovery rather than task time alone?

directions.br_entry: Replay real control traces, compare assistance policies and design tests around disagreement, recovery and user preference.

directions.title: Closed-loop neural control
directions.changed: Bidirectional interfaces now read state and change stimulation or feedback quickly enough to alter ongoing behavior.
directions.open: A closed loop can become unstable when state is partly observed, outcomes are delayed and both the user and neural system adapt.

anchors.title: A brain-computer interface that evokes tactile sensations improves robotic arm control
Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface
Long-term wireless streaming of neural recordings for circuit discovery and adaptive stimulation in individuals with Parkinson disease

questions.title: What state should close the loop?
How can control remain stable under delay, uncertainty and changing dynamics?
When should the loop adapt, abstain or ask for help?

directions.br_entry: Build explicit system models, simulate failure modes, and compare policies before online deployment.

directions.title: Brain-spine and peripheral restoration
directions.changed: Brain-spine interfaces and brain-controlled muscle stimulation showed that damaged pathways can be bypassed to restore coordinated movement.
directions.open: It remains difficult to choose the right bypass point, coordinate stimulation with intent and distinguish immediate assistance from lasting recovery.

anchors.title: A brain-spine interface alleviating gait deficits after spinal cord injury in primates
Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface
Restoration of reaching and grasping movements through brain-controlled muscle stimulation in a person with tetraplegia

questions.title: Which interface point best bypasses a lesion for a given function?
How should cortical intent and spinal or peripheral stimulation be coordinated?
What predicts transfer from assisted movements to lasting recovery?

directions.br_entry: Integrate lesion anatomy, motor decoding and stimulation models, then rank the next human or animal validation.

directions.title: Real-world autonomy, safety and end-to-end design
directions.changed: Fully implanted and high-performance systems have begun to operate outside short laboratory sessions.
directions.open: Daily use can be limited by setup, fatigue, caregiver burden, hardware reliability, recalibration or loss of agency rather than decoder score.

anchors.title: Fully implanted brain-computer interface in a locked-in patient with ALS
High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface
Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface

questions.title: Which component actually limits daily use?
Which laboratory benchmarks predict unsupervised home performance?
How should performance, safety, maintainability and agency be traded as one objective?

directions.br_entry: Analyze end-to-end logs, map failure chains and choose system changes by functional value rather than component metrics.

behavior.title: Behavior and cognition
behavior.copy: Behavioral science can now track bodies, parse long recordings, standardize assays across laboratories, and run experiments at population scale. The harder problem is deciding which patterns reflect a stable computation rather than a task, context, or measurement artifact.
big_questions: What are the stable units of behavior beneath changing tasks, contexts and incentives?
Which experimental environments genuinely distinguish competing models of cognition?
When do artificial agents extend behavioral science, and when do they create a different phenomenon?

directions.title: Behavioral measurement from video, sensors and logs
directions.changed: Markerless pose estimation and multi-animal tracking turned video into a high-dimensional behavioral measurement rather than a source of hand-scored labels.
directions.open: Tracking accuracy does not settle what should be measured, which errors matter for the scientific claim, or how well a model transports across bodies, cameras and environments.

anchors.title: DeepLabCut: markerless pose estimation of user-defined body parts with deep learning
SLEAP: a deep learning system for multi-animal pose tracking
Geometric deep learning enables 3D kinematic profiling across species and environments

questions.title: Which measurements are stable enough to support an individual or cross-species claim?
How should tracking uncertainty propagate into downstream behavioral conclusions?
What information is lost when rich motion is reduced to a few familiar labels?

directions.br_entry: Audit existing recordings, compare measurement representations, and identify the smallest annotation or calibration set needed for a new analysis.

directions.title: Behavioral segmentation and hierarchy
directions.changed: Unsupervised and expert-guided systems can now divide continuous movement into recurring motifs at scale.
directions.open: A segmentation can be reproducible yet scientifically arbitrary; boundaries, timescales and hierarchies often change with the model and the recording setup.

anchors.title: Keypoint-MoSeq: parsing behavior by linking point tracking to pose dynamics
B-SOiD, an open-source unsupervised algorithm for identification and fast prediction of behaviors
A-SOiD, an active-learning platform for expert-guided, data-efficient discovery of behavior

questions.title: What makes a behavioral unit useful rather than merely clusterable?
At which timescale do motifs become predictive of neural state, context or outcome?
Can a hierarchy learned in one setting be recognized in another without forcing the same labels?

directions.br_entry: Compare segmentation families on held-out recordings and score them by prediction, perturbation sensitivity and expert utility rather than visual plausibility alone.

directions.title: Latent states and strategy switching
directions.changed: State-space analyses showed that apparent lapses and variability can reflect persistent changes in strategy rather than independent trial noise.
directions.open: Latent states are easy to over-interpret, and several different models can explain the same choices and reaction times.

anchors.title: Mice alternate between discrete strategies during perceptual decision-making
Keypoint-MoSeq: parsing behavior by linking point tracking to pose dynamics
Standardized and reproducible measurement of decision-making in mice

questions.title: When does a latent state correspond to a distinct strategy rather than a flexible fit?
Which observations can distinguish gradual learning from abrupt state switching?
Do the same states recur across days, tasks and subjects?

directions.br_entry: Fit competing state models, test counterfactual predictions, and choose task manipulations that force the models to disagree.

directions.title: Learning, adaptation and non-stationarity
directions.changed: Longitudinal assays and representation learning made it possible to follow how behavior changes within and across sessions.
directions.open: Improvement can reflect learning, fatigue, changed motivation, strategy discovery or adaptation to the measurement itself.

anchors.title: Mice alternate between discrete strategies during perceptual decision-making
Standardized and reproducible measurement of decision-making in mice
Learnable latent embeddings for joint behavioural and neural analysis

questions.title: What is being learned: the task, a strategy, a motor routine or the experimenter?
Which changes persist after the incentive, context or interface is removed?
How should an experiment adapt without changing the construct it aims to measure?

directions.br_entry: Decompose longitudinal trajectories, compare change-point and continuous-learning models, and propose the next session that best separates them.

directions.title: Naturalistic and continuous behavior
directions.changed: Large-scale video and neural recordings showed that ongoing movement explains substantial variance that trial summaries leave behind.
directions.open: Natural behavior is rich but poorly controlled, so correlation can be driven by shared context, measurement density or unobserved goals.

anchors.title: Single-trial neural dynamics are dominated by richly varied movements
Spontaneous behaviors drive multidimensional, brainwide activity
DeepLabCut: markerless pose estimation of user-defined body parts with deep learning

questions.title: Which dimensions of natural behavior are causally relevant to neural activity or outcome?
How can continuous behavior be aligned to events without inventing arbitrary trial boundaries?
What survives when the same behavior is observed in a new environment?

directions.br_entry: Build synchronized behavioral representations, test event definitions and nuisance controls, and identify interventions that turn correlation into a discriminating experiment.

directions.title: Games and virtual worlds as experimental environments
directions.changed: Games can provide persistent rules, repeated choices, social interaction and controllable interventions at a scale that conventional tasks rarely reach.
directions.open: Game mechanics can become part of the phenomenon, and a pattern that predicts play may not generalize to the construct researchers hoped to measure.

anchors.title: Global determinants of navigation ability
People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games

questions.title: When can a game support causal behavioral science rather than descriptive telemetry?
Which game manipulation most cleanly separates competing models of learning, planning or cooperation?
Which behavioral regularities survive outside the game that produced them?

directions.br_entry: Translate game events into explicit hypotheses, replay natural experiments, and design small interventions with predeclared behavioral readouts.

directions.title: Population-scale digital experiments
directions.changed: Mobile and online platforms made it possible to collect behavioral data across countries, ages and social settings at unprecedented scale.
directions.open: Large samples amplify selection bias, device effects, unequal exposure and shallow measurements as easily as they amplify signal.

anchors.title: Global determinants of navigation ability
Experimental evidence for tipping points in social convention
Many Labs 2: investigating variation in replicability across samples and settings
anchors.venue: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science

questions.title: Which population patterns survive reweighting, device controls and independent samples?
How should a digital task be calibrated across cultures and levels of familiarity?
What can a very large but narrow measure establish about cognition?

directions.br_entry: Audit sampling and measurement shift, reproduce headline effects under alternative population models, and identify the smaller confirmatory study that is still needed.

directions.title: Individual differences and longitudinal behavior
directions.changed: Repeated behavioral data made within-person dynamics and stable individual structure jointly measurable.
directions.open: A person-level score can be reliable but uninformative, or predictive only because it captures context, practice or demographics.

anchors.title: Large-scale analysis of test-retest reliabilities of self-regulation measures
Mice alternate between discrete strategies during perceptual decision-making
Standardized and reproducible measurement of decision-making in mice

questions.title: Which behavioral features are stable enough to characterize a person?
When does a population model fail in a systematic subset of people?
Can within-person change be predicted without confusing it with regression to the mean?

directions.br_entry: Separate within- and between-person effects, measure repeatability against matched baselines, and look for boundary conditions rather than one universal persona.

directions.title: Social and collective behavior
directions.changed: Digital traces and multi-animal tracking made interaction networks and group dynamics observable at fine temporal resolution.
directions.open: Individual preference, social influence and shared environment are difficult to separate, especially when the network changes in response to behavior.

anchors.title: Experimental evidence for tipping points in social convention
SLEAP: a deep learning system for multi-animal pose tracking

questions.title: When is a group pattern caused by social influence rather than assortative exposure?
Which interaction features predict coordination, conflict or collective error?
How should an intervention be targeted when it changes both people and the network between them?

directions.br_entry: Compare causal graph and agent-based explanations, exploit timing and network perturbations, and design tests around predicted disagreements.

directions.title: Cross-laboratory behavioral reproducibility
directions.changed: Coordinated protocols showed that complex animal behavior can be measured consistently across laboratories when hardware, training and analysis are made explicit.
directions.open: Standardization can conceal local adaptations, and a replicated average may coexist with different strategies or failure modes in each site.

anchors.title: Standardized and reproducible measurement of decision-making in mice
Many Labs 2: investigating variation in replicability across samples and settings
anchors.venue: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science

questions.title: Which parts of a behavioral assay must be standardized, and which should vary to test transport?
Does the same average performance arise from the same strategy across laboratories?
What is the smallest shared protocol that still supports a common claim?

directions.br_entry: Decompose site effects, compare latent strategies, and define transport tests that preserve scientifically meaningful heterogeneity.

directions.title: Cross-species computational variables
directions.changed: Common tracking, task and latent-representation tools made behavior more directly comparable across species.
directions.open: Similar movements or task scores do not guarantee the same computation, and species-specific sensory and motivational structure can invalidate a neat mapping.

anchors.title: Geometric deep learning enables 3D kinematic profiling across species and environments
Learnable latent embeddings for joint behavioural and neural analysis
Standardized and reproducible measurement of decision-making in mice

questions.title: Which computational variables can be compared meaningfully across species?
When is a cross-species mismatch evidence about mechanism rather than failed translation?
What task redesign would make the human and animal hypotheses genuinely commensurate?

directions.br_entry: Align models at the level of predictions rather than labels, search existing cross-species datasets, and identify the experiment that tests a shared computation.

directions.title: Adaptive and closed-loop experiment design
directions.changed: Active learning and online behavioral systems can now choose the next trial, stimulus or annotation based on what has already been observed.
directions.open: An adaptive design can optimize a convenient proxy, oversample unusual subjects, or make the final statistical target difficult to interpret.

anchors.title: A-SOiD, an active-learning platform for expert-guided, data-efficient discovery of behavior
SLEAP: a deep learning system for multi-animal pose tracking
People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games

questions.title: Which next trial would most reduce uncertainty between the competing behavioral models?
How should an adaptive experiment account for participant learning and fatigue?
When does personalization improve inference, and when does it destroy comparability?

directions.br_entry: Simulate policies against competing generative models, preserve a valid estimand, and freeze stopping rules before prospective use.

directions.title: Synthetic participants and foundation models of cognition
directions.changed: Language models have been used to simulate survey and experimental responses, while cross-task behavioral models have begun to predict choices across many paradigms.
directions.open: Plausible answers can come from task familiarity, semantic cues or population stereotypes rather than a human-like cognitive structure.

anchors.title: Using large language models to simulate multiple humans and replicate human subject studies
A foundation model to predict and capture human cognition

questions.title: Does a synthetic participant recover task-to-task relationships and individual variation, not only average responses?
Which prompt labels or cover stories become unintended causal variables?
When should a model abstain because the human population or task is outside its calibrated range?

directions.br_entry: Run label swaps, persona ablations, contamination probes and human-ceiling comparisons before using synthetic participants to guide a real experiment.

mechanisms.title: Circuits, cells and biological models
mechanisms.copy: Cell atlases, large-scale recordings, connectomes, all-optical perturbation and human-derived models have turned mechanism into a multiscale, data-linked problem. The aim is not to describe every scale separately, but to find explanations that survive between them.
big_questions: How do measurements at one biological scale constrain mechanisms at another?
Which causal perturbation would most clearly separate the competing explanations?
Can predictive models choose better experiments, rather than merely fit experiments already performed?

directions.title: Cell types and molecular identity
directions.changed: Multimodal cell censuses linked transcription, epigenetics, anatomy and physiology in a common taxonomy.
directions.open: A cell-type label does not by itself explain function, state dependence, developmental origin or vulnerability in disease.

directions.br_entry: Resolve cell ontologies across datasets, connect type annotations to functional evidence, and prioritize perturbations that separate competing roles.

directions.title: Spatial omics and tissue organization
directions.changed: Whole-brain spatial atlases placed molecular identity back into anatomical neighborhoods and gradients.
directions.open: Spatial association can reflect developmental geometry, cell composition or technical resolution rather than a functional interaction.

At what resolution do molecular gradients become distinct biological compartments?
How should spatial omics be aligned with imaging, connectivity and perturbation data?

directions.br_entry: Integrate spatial datasets, test composition-aware alternatives, and nominate regions or boundaries for targeted measurement.

directions.title: Structural connectomics
directions.changed: Dense electron-microscopy reconstructions now span complete fly brains, substantial mammalian tissue volumes and human cortical samples.
directions.open: A wiring diagram is incomplete without synaptic sign, strength, dynamics, state and a way to tell which motifs matter for computation.

How much of a circuit can be compressed without losing the computation of interest?
Which apparent species differences reflect scale or sampling rather than a different circuit principle?

directions.br_entry: Search connectomes for motif-level hypotheses, compare them with functional data, and identify the smallest causal test of a structural prediction.

directions.title: Functional connectomics
directions.changed: Paired large-scale physiology and ultrastructure made it possible to relate responses, connectivity and cell morphology in the same tissue.
directions.open: Structure-function relationships remain many-to-many, and sampled activity covers only a fraction of the states a circuit can enter.

directions.br_entry: Fit competing structure-function models, test them on held-out neurons or stimuli, and rank experiments by expected disagreement.

directions.title: Neural population dynamics
directions.changed: High-density recording and latent-state methods revealed low-dimensional trajectories within very high-dimensional neural activity.
directions.open: Similar latent geometry can arise from different mechanisms, and the most predictive representation is not necessarily the one the circuit uses.

directions.br_entry: Compare dynamical models on prediction and intervention, align populations across recordings, and search for perturbations that produce divergent trajectories.

directions.title: Brain-wide distributed computation
directions.changed: Simultaneous recordings across many regions showed that sensation, choice, movement and internal state are distributed more broadly than canonical pathways imply.
directions.open: Broad activity can reflect shared movement, arousal or common drive; distributed correlation does not establish which regions are necessary or computationally distinct.

directions.title: Causal read-write experiments
directions.changed: Closed-loop and holographic optical methods made it possible to identify an ensemble and perturb selected cells during ongoing behavior.
directions.open: Artificial activation can produce a behavior without showing that the same ensemble normally causes it, and readout, stimulation and network compensation interact.

directions.title: Cell-type and projection-specific perturbation
directions.changed: Modern genetic and optical tools can perturb defined cell classes, projections and ensembles with fine timing.
directions.open: Specificity at the tool level does not guarantee specificity at the circuit level because recurrent networks, compensatory paths and behavioral state reshape the effect.

directions.title: Development, plasticity and recovery
directions.changed: Cell atlases and longitudinal models made developmental trajectories and post-injury reorganization more observable across scales.
directions.open: Cross-sectional snapshots are often mistaken for trajectories, and repaired function can emerge through a different circuit than the one used before injury.

directions.br_entry: Integrate longitudinal and cross-sectional evidence, compare trajectory models, and select measurements that can distinguish restoration from compensation.

directions.title: Cross-species conservation and divergence
directions.changed: Shared cell-taxonomy and multimodal atlas projects made homologous cell classes and circuits directly comparable across species.
directions.open: Molecular similarity, anatomical correspondence and computational equivalence can disagree, especially between model organisms and humans.

directions.title: Human observation to circuit hypothesis
directions.changed: Network mapping, comparative atlases and brain-wide recordings created a practical path from human imaging or behavior to candidate circuits and perturbations.
directions.open: A human association usually underdetermines cell type, direction of influence, temporal dynamics and the animal task that would test it.

directions.title: Organoids, assembloids and human-derived models
directions.changed: Human stem-cell models now reproduce aspects of cell diversity, network activity, regional interaction and disease phenotypes that were previously inaccessible.
directions.open: Maturation, vascularization, sensory input, batch effects and uncertain correspondence to in-vivo development limit what these systems can establish.

directions.title: Disease mechanisms and model validity
directions.changed: Patient-derived cells and organoids can express molecular, developmental and network phenotypes tied to specific disorders or genotypes.
directions.open: A phenotype in a model may be reproducible yet unrelated to symptoms, treatment response or the causal process in the intact nervous system.

directions.title: Predictive biological models and digital twins
directions.changed: Connectomes, cell atlases and large neural datasets made it plausible to build models that predict responses to new stimuli or perturbations.
directions.open: A model can interpolate recorded data while failing on causal interventions, new biological states or another preparation.

directions.title: Automated and information-efficient experimentation
directions.changed: Machine vision, active learning and closed-loop stimulation can now automate parts of behavioral and circuit experiments.
directions.open: Automation can increase throughput without improving question choice, and optimization can exploit fragile assay features or silently narrow the biology.

intervention.title: Intervention, repair and therapy

directions.title: Causal target discovery
directions.changed: Lesion networks, stimulation maps and convergent circuit analyses made treatment targets less dependent on a single anatomical coordinate.
directions.open: A convergent map can still mix causal, compensatory and epiphenomenal signals, and the relevant target may change with symptom, state and intervention type.

directions.title: Biomarkers and state estimation
directions.changed: Long-term neural sensing and symptom-linked biomarkers made it possible to estimate clinically relevant states outside a brief laboratory visit.
directions.open: Biomarkers can drift, become treatment-contingent or track a correlate rather than the state that should control therapy.

directions.changed: Predictive modeling and circuit-guided trials made differential treatment response an explicit research target.

directions.changed: New stimulation geometries, individualized targeting and direct circuit measurements expanded the range of non-invasive neuromodulation strategies.

directions.title: Invasive and adaptive neuromodulation
directions.changed: Implanted sensing-stimulation systems can adjust treatment using neural state rather than deliver a fixed schedule.

directions.title: Closed-loop intervention
directions.changed: Personalized systems have linked ongoing neural measurements to treatment delivery in movement and psychiatric disorders.

directions.changed: Brain-spine interfaces and targeted spinal stimulation restored useful movement by bypassing or re-engaging damaged pathways.

directions.changed: Wearable sensing, adaptive tasks and stimulation-assisted rehabilitation made training trajectories measurable and modifiable session by session.

directions.changed: Mechanism-rich imaging and modern trials made it possible to study how pharmacology changes circuits, behavior and the response to other interventions.

directions.changed: RNA replacement, gene transfer and stem-cell transplantation have moved from disease models into human trials and approved therapies for selected neurological conditions.

directions.changed: Accelerated protocols, model-guided targeting and adaptive stimulation made intervention parameters searchable rather than fixed by convention.

directions.changed: Home sensing, long-term implants and extended follow-up made it possible to observe treatment outside the controlled setting in which it was developed.
